basic_identification.full_title: Hydraulic Power Sprayers — Specification (First Revision) (द्रवचालित पावर स्प्रेयर — विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))

scope.summary: This standard prescribes the technical specifications, performance limits, material requirements, and methods of sampling and test for hydraulic power sprayers (including engine-operated and motor-operated knapsack, portable, and trolley-mounted sprayers) used in agriculture, horticulture, forestry, and public health spraying operations.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Food and Agriculture / Agricultural Machinery)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) to print on product nameplates as a certified assurance of quality, safety, and mechanical performance. Additionally, compliance with IS 11313 is strictly mandated under central and state agricultural department subsidy schemes (such as the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization - SMAM) and public procurement tenders across India.

requirements.detail: The standard mandates that when tested in accordance with Clause 8.4, the pump of the hydraulic power sprayer must achieve a volumetric efficiency of not less than 85 percent to limit internal slip and ensure stable pressure delivery.

Under Amendment No. 1 (August 2021), a previous note requesting members to suggest a minimum volumetric efficiency for roller vane pumps is deleted, confirming the standard's performance boundaries [1].

Amendment No. 1 (August 2021) inserts a precise mathematical formula to calculate the pump's power requirement: Power Required (P_req) = (rho * g * q * h) / 1000 kW, where rho is density of fluid (kg/m3), g is gravity (9.81 m/s2), q is discharge (m3/s), and h is differential head (m); or simply Power Required (P_req) = p * q [1].

All components in contact with agricultural spraying chemicals (such as pump cylinders, pistons, manifolds, suction chambers, and valves) must be constructed from corrosion-resistant materials (such as brass, stainless steel, or engineering polymers) to prevent chemical degradation.

The manufacturer must declare the sprayer's rated speed, rated pressure, discharge rate, and pump suction capacity. The actual discharge rate must conform to the declared rating within tight tolerance limits under the specified working head.
The pump must be tested under maximum achievable pressure (typically 20-30 kg/cm² or higher) and must show no leakage, joint sweating, or structural failure.
The sprayer must undergo a continuous running endurance test (typically 48 hours) to verify mechanical durability under full load, showing no seal degradation or cracks.
Appropriate protective wear (including hand gloves and face shields) must be specified in the instruction manual and supplied during operation to protect handlers from toxic chemical mists.

Any observed or calculated test or dimension value expressing discharge, pressure, or efficiency must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11313 : 2007 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical, dimensional, and testing requirements for hydraulic power sprayers used in agriculture and public health. Developed under the Agricultural Machinery and Equipment Sectional Committee (FAD 11) and reaffirmed in 2022, this standard regulates both engine-operated and motor-operated sprayers (including knapsack and trolley designs). It mandates a minimum pump volumetric efficiency of 85%, outlines strict material requirements to prevent chemical corrosion, and establishes high-pressure and 48-hour continuous running endurance tests. Active updates, such as Amendment No. 1 (August 2021), integrate a physics-based power formula to calculate pump hydraulic requirements, ensuring mechanical efficiency and user safety across India.
